chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Taymi, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Dawud ibn Abi Yazeed, from Ubayda ibn Bashir al-Khasha'i, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the cutter of the way (bandit), and I said, 'The people are saying that the Imam has a choice in it, to do whatever he desires.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is not whatever he desires, but he deals with them according to their crimes. The one who cuts the way, kills, and takes the property, his hand and leg are cut, and he is crucified. And the one who cuts the way, kills, and does not take the property, he is killed. And the one who cuts the way, takes the property, and does not kill, his hand and leg are cut (from opposite sides). And the one who cuts the way and does not take property and does not kill, he is exiled from the land.'
ai.seo_question: What are the specific penalties for highway robbers in Shia jurisprudence based on their actions?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies that the Imam’s discretion in applying the hadd of qat' al-tariq is bound by the specific elements of the crime, rejecting arbitrary judgment. It establishes a precise legal taxonomy where the combination of killing and theft results in crucifixion (surib), while lesser combinations result in execution or exile, reflecting the jurisprudential principles of proportionality in Shia fiqh. This ruling underscores the Imam's role as the authoritative interpreter of divine law, ensuring that penalties align strictly with the gravity of the offender's actions.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hassan Al Taymi, from Ali Bin Asbat, from Dawood Bin Abu Yazeed, from Ubeyda Bin Basheer Al Khash’amy who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the cutter of the way (bandit), and I said, ‘The people are saying that the Imam<sup>asws</sup> has a choice in it which thing he<sup>asws</sup> so desires to do’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It is not which thing he<sup>asws</sup> so desires to do, but he<sup>asws</sup> would deal with them in accordance with their crimes. The one who cuts off the way, so he kills and seizes the property, his hand and his leg would be cut, and he would be cruficified. And the one who cuts off the way, so he kills and does not seize the property, he would be killed. And the one who cuts off the way, and seizes the property, and does not kill, his hand and his leg would be cut (from opposite sides). And the one who cuts off the way and does not seize the property, and does not kill, he would be exiled from the land’.
